### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **36** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**12** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via AutomationServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class), getMetaItemLayered (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation), packageId (literal, a string literal in storedEntryRow))_
- `content/docs/deployment/app-dependencies.mdx`  _(via packageId (literal, a string literal in storedEntryRow))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via packageId (literal, a string literal in storedEntryRow))_
- `content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-chatbot.mdx`  _(via packageId (literal, a string literal in storedEntryRow))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via AutomationServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via packageId (literal, a string literal in storedEntryRow), getPublished (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.getPublished, bound to GET /api/v1/meta/:type/:name/published; the bare tail of client method meta.getPublished, bound to GET /meta/:type/:name/published))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via packageId (literal, a string literal in storedEntryRow))_
- `content/docs/permissions/capabilities.mdx`  _(via packageId (literal, a string literal in storedEntryRow))_
- `content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx`  _(via packageId (literal, a string literal in storedEntryRow))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`  _(via packageId (literal, a string literal in storedEntryRow))_
- `content/docs/ui/doc-pages.mdx`  _(via packageId (literal, a string literal in storedEntryRow))_

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via /:type/:name/published (route, bridged from symbol getMetaItemLayered — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class), resolveFlowPrecedence (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via packageId (literal, a string literal in storedEntryRow))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **16** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fa494d0538fe69e19be4a21ab13b92e8e6ae8d23` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bec0324a9826f761b8a9fd12b55038b7fab4aa59` — the merge of head `56a1fe5968aa39ff344b57455d578514c8bd7e12` into base `fa494d0538fe69e19be4a21ab13b92e8e6ae8d23`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bec0324a9826f761b8a9fd12b55038b7fab4aa59 && git checkout bec0324a9826f761b8a9fd12b55038b7fab4aa59
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fa494d0538fe69e19be4a21ab13b92e8e6ae8d23 56a1fe5968aa39ff344b57455d578514c8bd7e12 && git checkout -B drift-repro fa494d0538fe69e19be4a21ab13b92e8e6ae8d23 && git merge --no-ff 56a1fe5968aa39ff344b57455d578514c8bd7e12

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fa494d0538fe69e19be4a21ab13b92e8e6ae8d23
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fa494d0538fe69e19be4a21ab13b92e8e6ae8d23` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `0e67bba07873d54d3420d2d905334db3448da290`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #28412 (body; the triage record, the claim, the os-dev-report), this PR's body, its 23-file list and the net diff `main...0e67bba0`, and the 48 latest check-runs on the head: every one is `success` or `skipped`, none failed or pending (Check Changeset, Lint & Repo Gates, PM dispatch-gates, Test Core 1-8/8, Dogfood Regression Gate and Governed Surface Queue Guard all `success`). Those conclusions are the gate verdicts. Nothing was re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**Right, the widening the card asks for (Wanted 1-6):**
- **Save door opens `flow`, and only `flow`.** `isOpenOverrideType` (`protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts`) admits `flow` through `CONDITIONS_DELIVERED = {'flow'}` (`:230`), inside N-09's one gate. `judgeOverrideWrite` still requires the writer's `packageId` (the write address, never the body) to be the declared base's pair, inside the closure, with the base shipping the name. `action` still answers `declared_type_not_yet_available` (the cli pin moves that row to `action`). No second gate exists: `tenantAuthoredWriteRefusal` lifts the flow lock only on `overrideWriteVerdict(...).verdict === 'admit'`, which is the same gate. Correct.
- **View admission.** `declinesStoredRow(type, name, row)` (`protocol-lock-state.ts`) lets a shipped flow name's row through only when `isServedOverrideRowOf(row, owner)` holds. That is N-10's one predicate, judged on the row's `package_id` column: `storedEntryRow` maps `entry.packageId`, and the by-name and layered reads pass the raw stored record. No second predicate exists. Called without `row`, it answers the by-name decline as before. Correct.
- **Boot-pull binding comes from the column, not the body.** `hydrateOverlayIntoRegistry` records `options.packageId` (the column) as a non-enumerable `Symbol.for` property (`stored-row-binding.ts`). `classifyContender` reads only `storedRowBindingOf(item)`, never `_packageId`, and only inside a name the loader's set holds. A copy, a JSON body or a body-stamped `_packageId` carries no binding, so it admits nothing. The card's ⛔ on the body's `_packageId` holds, and the not-admitted pins cover it (a dependent's declaration, a package-less row stamping the pair, a body that only claims the pair, the pair's undeclared row, another base's pair).
- **Rank and ledger.** `override` (0) ranks over `package` (1) and `runtime` (2). An override over its own base writes no receipt. `packagedFlowOwner` and the flow name are unchanged, so the toggle door, the §7.3 subflow guard and `FLOW_DISABLED` key the override as the base (ledger off/on pinned, N-12 suspended-run case pinned). The four arming steps already go through `resolveFlowContenders`, and `registerFlow` rebinds in one step. Correct.
- **Remedy (Wanted 6).** The undeclared remedy and the sealed flow save sentence name the `.custom` declaration or a new name, not the clone. A delete still names the clone. Correct.
- **Public surface.** New exports `bindStoredRow` and `storedRowBindingOf` (metadata-protocol index). `FlowContender.source` (exported from service-automation) gains `'override'`. The changeset discloses both. service-automation already declares `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/spec`. Correct.

**Wrong: the /meta pair-row delete widens beyond the card (MUST-FIX).**
- `isPairRowRemoval` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts:257-263`) keys on `isOpenOverrideType`, so it applies to every open override type, not only `flow`: view, dashboard, report, translation, email_template, page, app, dataset, doc, book, mapping and flow. `deleteMetaItem` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:28298`, used at `:28367`, `:28390`, `:28624`) then skips `refusePackagedBaseRemoval`. Two shipped types are newly admitted:
  - `mapping` and `doc` are `supportsOverlay: false` and `allowEnvironmentOverlay: false`. On main, a /meta delete that names the pair of a shipped mapping or doc name is refused 403 `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` (sealed, and outside the #6960 carve-out). At this head it is admitted and sent to the store as `runtime-only`, which `allowRuntimeCreate: true` lets through.
  - For the overlay-capable open types, the delete receipt's `intent` changes from `override-artifact` to `runtime-only`, and the `_lock` delete gate now runs on that path.
- None of this is in the card (it opens `flow` alone). None of it is in the `Clause-②:` line or the changeset, which describe the delete as the flow override's. The code comment at `protocol.ts:28292-28297` says "(`flow`)". No test covers a non-flow pair-row delete. It is the narrowing direction, but it is an accept-set widening that is neither declared nor pinned.
- Fix, either way: (a) scope it to the types this change delivers. In `isPairRowRemoval`, require `CONDITIONS_DELIVERED.has(singular)` (or `singular === 'flow'`) in place of `isOpenOverrideType(singular)`, and add a pin that a `mapping` pair-row delete keeps its 403. Or (b) declare it. Name the delete widening for every open type in the `Clause-②:` line and the changeset, and pin a `mapping` or `doc` pair-row delete as admitted and a view's delete receipt intent. That second option rules on N-09 and N-10's surface, so it needs a ruling on the card first. (a) is the card's scope.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset sets `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/service-automation` to `minor`. That matches what the diff publishes: new exports, a widened accept set and a widened `FlowContender.source` union, with no spec key and no removal. The cli, cloud-connection, objectql, rest and runtime hunks are tests only, so they need no entry. Check Changeset is `success`.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the changeset, and the PR body's longer `Clause-②: yes (widening: ...)`, are the right direction. The text understates the published widening by the non-flow pair-row delete in ①. Once that delete is scoped to `flow` (fix a), the line is exact as written. Under fix (b), both carriers must name it.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none were filed. Nothing to answer.
- **Out-of-scope (b): the read envelope reports `deletable: false` for a served flow override while the /meta delete naming the pair is admitted.** Answered: the envelope follows the base's seal, and Studio is the consumer, so N-18 (#28570, Studio "Customize this flow") owns it. Accepted as carried, not a defect of this card's contract. The report says "noted, not filed", so the seat must record it on #28570 before landing. Otherwise the carrier does not know it holds it.
- **Out-of-scope (c): a package-less stored row beside the pair row can take the bare registry slot, so the boot pull sees it until `kernel:ready` re-arms the override from the view.** Answered: the window closes in the same boot, the gate now refuses new rows of that shape, and legacy rows are N-16's migration. Accepted as carried. As with (b), the seat must record it on N-16's card under #28236, because it was "noted, not filed".
- **Acceptance note: two code packages shipping one flow name.** Answered: the view's copies carry no binding, so the override ranks by the existing package rule there. That is outside D9's one-base-one-pair case, the card does not ask for it, and no test claims it. Accepted.
- **Acceptance note: a delete naming no package keeps the sealed refusal.** Confirmed in the code (`isPairRowRemoval` returns false without a `packageId`).
- **Dev flag: CI was not awaited at report time.** Resolved: all 48 latest check-runs on this head are `success` or `skipped`.

Must-fix before landing: the non-flow pair-row delete widening in ①. Fix (a) needs no ruling.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `56a1fe5968aa39ff344b57455d578514c8bd7e12`
Local-runs: none

This is a delta review. It follows the FAIL record 6559358939 on head `0e67bba0`.

Inputs: the compare `0e67bba0...56a1fe59`, which is 22 commits. Two are this PR's own: `44d55533` (the fix) and `56a1fe59` (a test after the merge). Merge `bac10f7b` brings in 19 main commits up to `c16040d8`. I also read an interdiff of the old net PR diff (`2678600d...0e67bba0`) against the new one (`c16040d8...56a1fe59`). Both hold the same 23 files. Every changed line is in `44d55533` or `56a1fe59`, so the merge left the PR's own hunks and its changeset as they were. Other inputs: card #28412 and its three comments, the PR body, carriers #28570, #28413 and #28717, and the 48 latest check-runs on the head. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**Must-fix from 6559358939 is closed (fix a).**
- `isPairRowRemoval` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts:260-267`) now returns false unless `CONDITIONS_DELIVERED.has(singular)`. That set is `{'flow'}` (`:230`). The `isOpenOverrideType` check stays as a second condition. Every other open type now gets main's delete verdict again: `view`, `dashboard`, `report`, `translation`, `email_template`, `page`, `app`, `dataset`, `doc`, `book` and `mapping`. `action` was already out.
- `deleteMetaItem` computes `pairRowRemoval` once (`protocol.ts:28308`), and three places read it: the sealed refusal (`:28377`), the lock-gate condition (`:28400`) and the receipt intent (`:28634`). For a non-flow type the value is now false, so all three behave as on main again. No other caller exists in the diff. `protocol.ts:391` is only the import.
- The widening is pinned. The new pins are in `packages/objectql/src/protocol-flow-custom-override.test.ts` and run on the real ObjectQL engine:
  - A `mapping` pair-row delete answers 403 `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` and keeps the row. This holds on both the host-config and the environment kernel.
  - A `view` pair-row delete reaches `SysMetadataRepository.delete` with `intent: 'override-artifact'`.
- The pins are not vacuous. In `OVERRIDE_TYPE_CLASSIFICATION` (`packages/spec/src/kernel/customization-package.ts:317-339`), `mapping` and `view` are both `listed`, which is `overridable` with no conditions. So `isOpenOverrideType` is true for both. If the old key came back, the mapping delete would be admitted and the view intent would be `runtime-only`, and the pins would go red.
- CI ran the pins. Test Core job `124903974668` shows `src/protocol-flow-custom-override.test.ts (7 tests)` green, up from 4 before.
- The fix needed no ruling. It is the card's own scope.

**Delta commit `56a1fe59`: the hydration pin follows main's #28594.**
- Main's `storedOverlayEntries` now serves `_packageId` from the `package_id` column. It replaces a body's own stamp or drops it. So the pin now expects `hydrated._packageId` to be the pair. The `storedRowBindingOf` assertion and the not-serialized assertion did not change. The `stored-row-binding.ts` header is now accurate.
- One side effect: on this read path, the protocol pins "a package-less row whose body stamps the pair" and the dependent's row no longer tell the symbol apart from `_packageId`, because both now say the same thing. The card's ⛔ (the binding is never read from the body's `_packageId`) is still pinned where it can be judged. `flow-precedence-loader-set.test.ts` feeds "a body that only CLAIMS the pair (no stored binding)" straight to `classifyContender` and expects no admission. So nothing is lost, and nothing needs fixing here.

**The rest of ①, as accepted in 6559358939, is unchanged.** Save-door admission, view admission, the boot-pull binding, rank and ledger, the remedy and the public surface (`bindStoredRow`, `storedRowBindingOf`, `FlowContender.source` gaining `'override'`) all match the old head line for line.

**Non-blocking prose nits.** Neither one is a declaration line.
- PR body line 29 still says the pair delete is admitted "of an open-override type". The tree now admits it for `flow` only. The seat should change it to "of a flow" before landing.
- The comment at `protocol.ts:28632` still says "The pair's row of an open-override type". The intent expression it sits on is correct, because `pairRowRemoval` is now flow-only.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset `.changeset/28412-flow-custom-override-armed.md` is unchanged by the delta. It sets `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` `minor` and `@objectstack/service-automation` `minor`. That still matches what is published: new exports, the `flow` accept-set widening and a widened `FlowContender.source` union. No spec key changes and nothing is removed. The delta takes away the undeclared non-flow delete widening and adds no surface. Its other hunks are tests and comments. Check Changeset is `success`.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the changeset, and the PR body's `Clause-②: yes (widening: ... and a /meta delete naming that pair removes its row; ...)`, say "that pair", meaning the flow save. 6559358939 said these lines are exact once fix (a) lands. Fix (a) has landed, so both carriers are exact as written.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions`:** none in the os-dev-report `6559023315`. No new dev report was posted for the delta. The commit messages of `44d55533` and `56a1fe59` state the change. Nothing to answer.
- **Out-of-scope (b), `deletable: false` on the served override's read envelope:** answered and now recorded. Seat 1 posted it on #28570 (N-18, open) as comment 6559375158, so the carrier holds it. This closes the "record it before landing" condition in 6559358939.
- **Out-of-scope (c), a package-less flow row can take the bare registry slot at boot:** answered and re-carried. Seat 1 recorded it on #28413 (N-16a) as comment 6559382296. N-16a's dev measured that the migration cannot remove the shape (report 6559681417): `flow` is not an overlay type, the shadowed shape is left alone, and a declared flow write was still refused there. Seat 3 then filed #28717 (p2, `pm:dispatched`, seat 1). That card asks for the declared override to win the bare slot from the first pull. #28413 is closed, but the flag's open carrier is #28717. Accepted as carried. It is not a defect of this card's contract, because the window closes in the same boot.
- **Acceptance note, two code packages shipping one flow name:** unchanged by the delta. Still accepted.
- **Acceptance note, a delete naming no package keeps the sealed refusal:** still true. `isPairRowRemoval` returns false when `packageId` is not a non-empty string.
- **Dev flag, CI not awaited:** resolved on this head. All 48 latest check-runs are complete: 35 `success` and 13 `skipped`. None is red or pending. Check Changeset, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Test Core 1-8/8, Dogfood Regression Gate, Live E2E UI, TypeScript Type Check and Governed Surface Queue Guard are all `success`. Those conclusions are the gate verdicts. The legacy commit-status API reads `pending` with zero statuses, which is not a check and gates nothing.
- **Note on the delta's evidence:** no ablation leg was recorded for the two new pins. Reading the code shows they go red if the old key comes back (see ①). This is a note, not a must-fix.
- **Author:** the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no author note is owed.

No must-fix remains on this head. Of the two nits in ①, the PR body sentence can be edited without moving the head. The `protocol.ts:28632` comment is in a code file, not a prose face. A commit for it moves the head and needs its own delta review, so it is better left to a later change that touches that file.
